title: TerraAlign: Language-Supervised Alignment of Vision and Proprioception for Multi-Grained Terrain Classification
abstract: Understanding terrain properties based on visual and proprioceptive sensor modalities is essential for safe locomotion and motion planning in unstructured environments, yet existing terrain classification methods primarily focus on coarse-grained material recognition. Fine-grained physical attributes such as unevenness that directly influence robot dynamics remain challenging to infer due to the heterogeneous characteristics of visual and proprioceptive modalities. In this paper, we propose TerraAlign, a language-supervised visual-proprioceptive alignment framework for unified coarse-to-fine terrain understanding. TerraAlign introduces language as a semantic bridge to align visual and inertial features into a shared embedding space, enabling consistent representation of both appearance and physical interaction properties. A contrastive alignment objective jointly optimizes cross-modal consistency, and a confidence-aware fusion strategy ensures robustness under modality degradation. Experiments on two datasets demonstrate that TerraAlign significantly improves performance in coarse-grained material classification and fine-grained unevenness prediction compared to state-of-the-art baselines, and highlight the effectiveness of language-supervised multimodal alignment for physically grounded terrain understanding in real-world robotic systems.

title: STaR: Scalable Task-Conditioned Retrieval for Long-Horizon Multimodal Robot Memory
abstract: Mobile robots are often deployed over long durations in diverse open, dynamic scenes, including indoor settings such as warehouses and manufacturing facilities, and outdoor settings such as agricultural and roadway operations. A core challenge is to build a scalable long-horizon memory that supports an agentic workflow for planning, retrieval, and reasoning over open-ended instructions at variable granularity, while producing precise, actionable answers for navigation. We present STaR, an agentic reasoning framework that (i) constructs a task-agnostic, multi-modal long-term memory that generalizes to unseen queries while preserving fine-grained environmental semantics (object attributes, spatial relations, and dynamic events), and (ii) introduces a Scalable Task-Conditioned Retrieval algorithm based on the Information Bottleneck principle to extract from long-term memory a compact, non-redundant, information-rich set of candidate memories for contextual reasoning. We evaluate STaR on NaVQA (mixed indoor/outdoor campus scenes) and WH-VQA, a customized warehouse benchmark with many visually similar objects built with Isaac Sim, emphasizing contextual reasoning. Across the two datasets, STaR consistently outperforms strong baselines, achieving higher success rates and markedly lower spatial error. We further deploy STaR on a real Husky wheeled robot in both indoor and outdoor environments, demonstrating robust long-horizon reasoning, scalability, and practical utility. title: DeNoise2Completion: Diffusion-Based Unified Model for Point Cloud Denoising and Completion
abstract: Adverse weather conditions (e.g., rain, snow) degrade LiDAR perception by introducing false echo noise and causing structural incompleteness. Addressing these issues is complicated by the unavailability of paired ground truth in real-world dynamic scenes, rendering standard supervised methods impractical. To this end, we propose DeNoise2Completion, a unified progressive framework for noise suppression and unsupervised target reconstruction. First, we introduce a Patch-based Range-Diffusion model for efficient denoising. By leveraging the spatial regularity of 2D range images to distinguish noise patterns, this module achieves 92.69% precision on the WADS dataset, establishing a clean geometric foundation. Second, for completion tasks without ground truth labels, we propose a retrieval-augmented voxel diffusion approach. Rather than relying on coarse global priors, we align partial observations with ShapeNet templates through voxelized feature matching of incomplete vehicle point cloud specific regions to obtain fine-grained guidance. Crucially, template incompleteness constraints and geometric inclusion constraints are employed during training to ensure reconstruction strictly follows observed sensor measurements. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework achieves excellent performance among unsupervised methods, robustly completing incomplete point clouds into full vehicles and improving downstream detection task accuracy (Chamfer distance 31.6), providing a robust solution for adverse weather perception.

title: Air-Ground Robotic Collaborative Reconstruction by Cross-View Depth Completion in Large-Scale Environment
abstract: Aerial depth reconstruction plays an important role in applications such as disaster assessment and city-scale digital twins. Although Unmanned Aerial Vehicles with a camera provide wide-area coverage and flexible viewpoints, monocular depth estimation alone often suffers from scale ambiguity and degraded accuracy in large-scale scenes. To address this challenge, we propose RefineNet, a cross-view air–ground collaborative framework for depth completion from monocular aerial images, enabling high-quality 3D reconstruction of large-scale scenes. It incorporates high-precision point clouds captured by Unmanned Ground Vehicles to provide reliable metric scale and geometric constraints for aerial depth prediction. To effectively fuse heterogeneous and sparse cross-view information, RefineNet adopts a multi-stage refinement strategy with confidence-aware depth integration, enabling robust utilization of ground depth cues while mitigating the influence of noise and occlusions. The proposed framework produces accurate dense depth predictions in a single forward pass without relying on computationally expensive optimization. Experiments are conducted on two synthetic benchmarks of varying scales and a real-world collaborative robotic dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that RefineNet consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across diverse scenes, while ablation studies further verify the contribution of each component to the overall system.

title: AsyncMDE: Real-Time Monocular Depth Estimation Via Asynchronous Spatial Memory
abstract: Foundation-model-based monocular depth estimation offers a viable alternative to active sensors for robot perception, yet its computational cost often prohibits deployment on edge platforms. Existing methods perform independent per-frame inference, wasting the substantial computational redundancy between adjacent viewpoints in continuous robot operation. This paper presents AsyncMDE, an asynchronous depth perception system consisting of a frozen foundation model and a lightweight fast path that amortizes the foundation model's computational cost over time. The foundation model periodically produces high-quality spatial features in the background, while the lightweight fast path runs asynchronously in the foreground, fusing cached memory with current observations through complementary fusion, outputting depth estimates, and autoregressively updating memory. This enables cross-frame feature reuse with bounded accuracy degradation. With 3.83M trainable fast-path parameters and a 97.5M frozen slow path, AsyncMDE's fast path operates at 237 FPS on an RTX 4090, recovering 77% of the accuracy gap to the foundation model. Across indoor static, dynamic, and synthetic extreme-motion benchmarks, AsyncMDE degrades predictably and reaches 161 FPS fast-path inference on a TensorRT-optimized Jetson AGX Orin, supporting real-time edge deployment.

title: Visual Autoregressive Modeling through Online Multi-Scale Preference Optimization for Low-Level Image Perception
abstract: Robotic systems depend on accurate visual perception (e.g., depth estimation, surface normal prediction, and canny detection) for navigation, manipulation, and scene understanding. Performing these diverse tasks with a single model is desirable for resource-constrained robotic platforms, yet most approaches rely on task-specific architectures. Visual Autoregressive (VAR) models offer fast, parallel-friendly generation through next-scale prediction but remain underexplored for perception. We introduce Perception-VAR, a VAR-based framework that bridges generative modeling and perceptual understanding for robotic vision. We enhance image-conditioned generation with multi-scale DINOv2 conditioning to capture contextual semantics and geometric consistency across scales. To further align generation with perception, we develop a novel online multi-scale direct preference optimization algorithm that computes region-global rewards based on uncertainty at intermediate and final decoding scales, thereby imposing supervision on structurally ambiguous regions. This transforms preference learning into a process-aware refinement that progressively improves structural alignment throughout autoregressive decoding. Extensive experiments across depth estimation, surface normal prediction, and canny detection demonstrate that Perception-VAR consistently outperforms existing autoregressive approaches while offering favorable inference efficiency, demonstrating promise for real-time robotic perception.

title: CLEAR-IR: Clarity-Enhanced Active Reconstruction of Infrared Imagery for Low-Light Enhancement
abstract: This paper presents CLEAR-IR (Clarity Enhanced Active Reconstruction of Infrared Imagery), a novel framework for enabling robust robotic perception in dark environments using active infrared (IR) sensing. IR streams are less susceptible to noise than RGB in low light conditions but are dominated by structured light emitter patterns that hinder high level tasks such as object detection, tracking, and localisation. CLEAR-IR addresses this by reconstructing clean, RGB styled images from emitter populated IR inputs using a dual stream architecture inspired by DeepMAO [1], enabling standard RGB trained vision pipelines to operate without visible light. Evaluation across object detection, ArUco marker detection, and visual SLAM demonstrates that CLEARIR produces reliable perception in conditions ranging from well lit to completely dark, where passive RGB based enhancement methods fail entirely due to the physical absence of sensor signal.

title: Repurposing RGB-Based Foundation Model for Depth Estimation on Thermal Images Using Hierarchical Supervision
abstract: Depth estimation from thermal images is highly valuable for robotic applications in adverse conditions, such as nighttime and rainy weather. Recent studies have sought to transfer knowledge from RGB-based foundation models to thermal modalities, yet the rich hierarchical representations these models encode remain underutilized. To address this limitation, we propose RGB-HS, a novel framework for thermal-image depth estimation that leverages hierarchical supervision from an RGB-based foundation model. Specifically, we first replace the baseline thermal encoder with a foundational model and introduce a parallel RGB branch that also employs a foundational model as an encoder of the same architecture, taking RGB images as input. The alignment is then performed across multiple levels between the tokens of the two encoders, allowing the thermal student branch to capture both structural precision and semantic abstraction from the RGB teacher branch. Furthermore, we introduce verification to refine the alignment process by weighting tokens from the RGB branch based on RGB image quality. Extensive experiments on the popular benchmark demonstrate that RGB-HS achieves competitive performance and more effectively exploits the representational capacity of RGB-based foundation models for depth estimation on thermal images.
